title: Apple Refused Touchscreen Macs for 15 Years. Why Now? 💻👆 #shorts
description:
Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro went on sale on 6 November 2026. For years Apple said no: in 2010 Steve Jobs argued that touching a vertical screen gets tiring fast, and the Mac was built around a precise mouse pointer with small buttons. What changed? Macs now run on the same kind of chips as iPads and can run iPad apps, macOS has become more touch-friendly, and Apple says apps like Microsoft 365, Notion and Canva are getting touch updates. Whether people will actually reach for the screen is the big question.

lines: For fifteen years, Apple refused to make a touchscreen Mac. This month, it finally did.
Back in 2010, Steve Jobs said touching a vertical screen gets tiring fast. Your arm just isn't made to hover in the air.
And the Mac was built for a precise mouse pointer, with tiny buttons. Fingers are a lot bigger than a cursor.
What changed? Macs now use the same kind of chips as iPads, and can run iPad apps. And apps like Notion and Canva are getting touch updates.
Now the big question: will you actually reach up and touch it, or keep using the trackpad?
